verdict: PASS (scoped): physical beacon placement, 14 focused logical checks, remote GPU evidence and transition checks · FAIL: desktop visibility, full catalogue CI (580/581), independent commercial/motion/performance gates
nextGap: Fix the independently reproduced stale frontend revision-marker catalogue CI assertion (expects v2 while shipped Tower declares v3), then evaluate beacon occlusion in desktop and guardian crown clearance using new same-state GPU comparisons. Continuous motion, independent Jusant/ASTRO BOT comparisons and intended-device FPS remain unverified.

iterations.title: Establish the real starting point
iterations.finding: The existing game is an autonomous 2D platformer. Its simulation already covers generation, combat, upgrades, guardians, restart and replay. The visual presentation is the main transformation target.
iterations.checks: All 14 original tower test files passed before implementation. Baseline screenshot captured in Chromium.

iterations.title: Make moving platforms tell the truth
iterations.finding: The old render snapshot showed the base position of a moving platform while collision used its tick-adjusted position. Corrected the snapshot to use the same effective platform position.
iterations.checks: Regression reproduced the mismatch, then passed across four tick positions; authoritative checksum unchanged.

iterations.title: Build the cast and the tower in parallel
iterations.finding: Separate builders produced articulated original characters, five tower biomes and a full-screen spectator HUD. The lead is integrating them with the running simulation before independent visual review.
iterations.checks: Character geometry, pose transforms and owned disposal checked; environment geometry and floor lifecycle checked. Integrated visual verdict remains open.

iterations.title: Run the integrated 3D expedition
iterations.finding: The actual AI game now renders the modeled tower, articulated cast, pickups, projectiles and camera in WebGL. Independent review is opening; no reference win is claimed.
iterations.checks: Chromium: no page or shader errors; simulation and rendering advance; camera controls work. Host self-test passes authority, privacy, recovery and restart checks. Software GPU render cost remains high.

iterations.title: Improve shapes, action cues and render cost
iterations.finding: Added articulated strikes, recoil and collapse; weathered facade masses, biome ledges and distant citadels; closer follow camera and more readable HUD. A fresh critic inspected four real viewport captures and still preferred the reference. Large geometry and mobile composition need another pass.
iterations.checks: Captured desktop follow/overview and both phone orientations with no page or shader errors. Rigid world batching preserves every triangle and reduces fixture color meshes from roughly 200 to 69–79. Software GPU frame times remain too slow for a performance pass.

iterations.title: Repair continuous-run contracts
iterations.finding: Independent correctness review reproduced rejected intermission snapshots, stale new-run audio, consumed event accumulation, recovery that remained latched, and malformed request handling. Those server-side defects are fixed; browser cache restoration and audio races are being fixed separately.
iterations.checks: Six regression cases failed before their fixes and pass afterward. Moving-platform/action snapshot checks and the stream host authority, privacy, bounded replay, recovery and restart self-test pass.

iterations.title: Rebuild the main forms and reveal the climber
iterations.finding: Replaced the broad cylinder with an asymmetric fortress, framed the current sector, and moved the follow camera toward the climber’s eye line. The fresh critic now finds the desktop hero coherent and readable, while still preferring the reference for world and cast finish. Phone captions and vitals have measured clearance.
iterations.checks: All 73 Tower tests pass. Character batching preserves articulated geometry and reduces the climber from 53 to 10 mesh draws, enemies from 52–54 to 7. Actual desktop/phone captures render without shader errors. Stronger WebGL context-restoration testing exposed a remaining stall; investigation is active.

iterations.title: Repair graphics restoration and client lifecycle
iterations.finding: The independent correctness findings are fixed, including browser-cache restoration, sound races, run-boundary audio reset and lifecycle revisions. A stronger real-WebGL test reproduced invalid old GPU handles after context restoration; resources now retire before the context generation changes.
iterations.checks: Eight independent correctness probes passed. The two strengthened WebGL tests passed after the repair, including repeated context loss, intervening floor changes, preference preservation and zero GL errors. These results precede the later reflection-lighting pass.

iterations.title: Give the Foundry a working industrial identity
iterations.finding: Rebuilt the sector around unequal tapered pylons, a recessed furnace iris, ceramic shells, metal ribs and curved open platform brackets. Finished the cast with rounded armor and articulated poses. The separate critic finds the route clearer, while the commercial reference still wins.
iterations.checks: Structural clearance and real collider-aligned hazard geometry are covered by focused tests. The displayed image is actual game output from an unmodified authoritative tick-118 snapshot held for appearance review; it does not demonstrate live motion.

iterations.title: Expose the remaining motion gap
iterations.finding: The autonomous host and browser DOM progressed through genuine results, intermissions and restarts, but the inspected recordings remained on early gameplay images. No visual action, guardian performance, lifecycle or smoothness pass is awarded.
iterations.checks: The critic retained failed recordings and source hashes. Long frame intervals are no longer discarded by diagnostics. Original stone textures and bounded reflection lighting are being reviewed, and a separate builder is investigating render freshness and pacing.

iterations.title: Make recovery and measurements honest
iterations.finding: A fresh critic found and rechecked final shadow cleanup and partial reflection-conversion failures. Optional reflection failure now keeps direct lighting available. HTTP updates no longer claim live graphics when renderer submissions stop; accepted and submitted snapshots are distinguished.
iterations.checks: Final build, all 103 Tower logical tests and the stream-host self-test pass. Empty frame statistics are unknown rather than zero; real long visible intervals are retained. A bounded GPU-pacing experiment still produced no usable pixels, so no unproven pacing policy was shipped.

iterations.title: Inspect the final source without hiding the gaps
iterations.finding: Both strong WebGL recovery tests pass, with ready stone and reflection resources after two lost-context floor changes and no final GL error. Final Foundry and restored Storm output were captured. A fresh critic still prefers the reference; the portrait image visibly reports a graphics delay and covers the play area.
iterations.checks: 103 logical tests, build and host self-test pass. Final desktop/portrait captures report no browser errors. The portrait used explicit high quality at DPR 1. Stills and recovery checks do not prove continuous motion, successful phone play or a commercial-benchmark win.

iterations.title: Clear the gameplay view and stage the next encounter
iterations.finding: All three independent critics prefer the new image in the randomized blind before/after comparison. The HUD now uses compact vitals and icon controls; intent and telemetry are optional. Hostile armor and close encounter framing make character roles clearer. ASTRO BOT still wins the source-known commercial comparison.
iterations.checks: Thirteen real browser captures saved with zero page/GL errors. The eight additional captures used stable source hashes; these exposed a portrait camera gap and real caption/card overlap. A paused-callback fault confirms compact retained-delay treatment. One stepped real attack edge is pose evidence, not live motion.

iterations.title: Return real image failures to the builders
iterations.finding: Actual captures confirm separate upgrade/caption space, retained danger/recovery notices, readable health fill and a visible nearby guardian face. Sentinel grip/head separation improves. A fresh blind phone comparison exposed that the actual leftward landing remains hard to identify; the target cue blends with permanent moving-platform trim.
iterations.checks: 7/7 new browser layout/accessibility checks pass. Second-pass logical checks: cast 10/10, composition/world/resources 21/21, HUD/client/presentation 32/32. Ten of 11 requested images saved with stable hashes and zero page/GL errors; the high-quality desktop Ruins screenshot timed out. No full motion or commercial-bar win.

iterations.title: Clarify the landing and the reaching pose
iterations.finding: Fresh blind review prefers the new phone frame and correctly reads upward-left movement. The raised hand now separates from the hero at both jump directions; a correctly timed 100 ms strike reads as a forward jab. The guardian hammer has a distinct grip, shaft and head. Exact landing certainty and crown clearance remain open.
iterations.checks: All 129 Tower logical tests and 19 browser cases pass, including repeated real graphics recovery across floor changes. Build and host self-test pass. Six final images have matching source hashes and zero page/GL errors. No full motion or commercial-bar win.

iterations.title: Separate the intended landing from competing decks
iterations.finding: Preserved concurrent camera/HUD/cast work from 05d3633. Added one depth-tested, outlined double-chevron above the real intended landing. It follows effective moving-platform coordinates, is not a pickup or collision surface, and clears when traversal intent ends. The earlier local camera replacement was discarded rather than overwriting concurrent work.
iterations.checks: Two focused regressions failed before implementation; 13 focused composition/resource tests, build, all 130 Tower logical tests and host authority/privacy/recovery/restart self-test pass. Local managed Chromium blocks navigation; GitHub same-state before/after captures and real traversal-retirement/recovery checks are added but not yet verified. Self-review only: connected subagent workspace unavailable. Overall visual gate FAIL/unverified.

iterations.title: Bring the destination glyph back onto the real landing
iterations.finding: Downloaded and directly inspected the successful Gauntlet 15 Tower Landing Evidence artifact (run 41168718432, ID 13029769123). Six actual PNGs show a visible two-chevron marker, but in both portrait directions it hovers near/past the outer ledge rather than over the deck: the code placed it at radius 27.24 while the physical walking top spans 22.4–27.18. Moved only its presentation anchor to radial center 24.8, preserving the target ID, effective moving position, depth testing, fixed sixteen-triangle geometry and authority checksums. Actual evidence shows the trade-off: a more central, physically grounded beacon on both phones, but partial right-side obstruction by the tower upright in the desktop leftward screenshot. No complete desktop clearance is claimed.
iterations.checks: New GPU run 41172970087 at source d9ab916 succeeded and downloadable artifact 13031761634 contains six 390×844/960×600 held baseline/candidate PNGs and diagnostics: pinned checksums unchanged (tick379 cdb269d8, tick234 7a87ca02), zero page/GL errors, 16-triangle depth-tested beacon at radius 24.8. Direct self-inspection: both portrait destinations are more centrally identified; desktop leftward glyph is partly occluded by a tower upright. SCOPED PASS: geometry, movement retirement, screenshots present. SCOPED FAIL: full desktop occlusion-free target readability not proved. Tower Realism run 41172970019 is FAIL, 580/581 logical tests, stale catalogue frontend revision-marker expectation; no overall Gauntlet or performance pass. Original local focused 14/14 tests, build, host contract pass; wider local Tower suite timed out after case 122.
